# Bento notes sync protocol (v1)

Server: `bento-sync` (Rust, `server/`), deployed at `https://bento.radian.dk` behind nginx.
Single user, single shared bearer token. All timestamps are Unix **milliseconds**.

## Note object

```json
{
  "id": "6F1C2D3E-....",          // UUID string, generated by the client
  "body": "# Title\n\nmarkdown…",  // full markdown text of the note
  "created_at": 1761000000000,
  "updated_at": 1761000123456,     // client clock at last local edit
  "deleted": false,                // tombstone; body is "" when deleted
  "seq": 42,                       // server-assigned, strictly increasing per change (absent in client puts)
  "device": "MacBook-Pro",         // device that made the last change
  "meta": {}                       // opaque JSON object for client extras (e.g. {"pinned":true}); max 4 KB
}
```

`meta` keys used by the Notes client: `pinned` (bool), `pinOrder` (number, order within
pinned notes), `trashedAt` (ms; set when moved to Recently Deleted, purged after 60 days by
turning the note into a tombstone), `conflictOf` (id of the note this one is a
"conflicted copy" of: when a client's unsynced edit loses last-writer-wins to a
different text from another device, the client keeps its losing text as a new note
titled "‹title› (conflicted copy, ‹device›)" instead of discarding it). Unknown
keys must be preserved.

`body` max size 1 MB. The title is derived by clients (first non-empty line, markdown stripped); the server never parses `body`.

## Auth

Every request carries `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. (`?token=<token>` is also accepted for manual testing.)
Wrong/missing token → HTTP 401 (WebSocket upgrade refused with 401).

## REST

| Method | Path | Body | Response |
|---|---|---|---|
| GET | `/v1/health` | – | `{"ok":true,"seq":<latest seq>}` (no auth) |
| GET | `/v1/notes?since=<seq>` | – | `{"notes":[Note…],"seq":<latest seq>}` – all notes (incl. tombstones) with `seq > since`, ascending |
| PUT | `/v1/notes/<id>` | Note (no `seq`) | `{"note":Note,"accepted":true}` or `{"note":<stored Note>,"accepted":false}` |
| DELETE | `/v1/notes/<id>?updated_at=<ms>` | – | same as PUT with `deleted:true, body:""` |

## WebSocket: `GET /v1/sync` (upgrade)

Client → server:

```json
{"type":"hello","since":<last seq the client has applied>,"device":"MacBook-Pro"}
{"type":"put","note":{…Note without seq…}}
{"type":"ping"}
```

Server → client:

```json
{"type":"snapshot","notes":[…],"seq":<latest>}         // reply to hello: everything with seq > since
{"type":"ack","id":"…","seq":43,"accepted":true}       // reply to the sender's put
{"type":"note","note":{…}}                              // a change made by another connection, or the
                                                        // stored winner when the sender's put was rejected
{"type":"pong"}
{"type":"error","message":"…"}
```

Server sends a WebSocket ping frame every 30 s; clients may also send `{"type":"ping"}`.

## Conflict rule (last writer wins)

A put for an existing id is **accepted** iff `put.updated_at >= stored.updated_at`
(ties: accepted). Accepted puts get `seq = ++global_seq`, are stored, acked to the
sender and broadcast as `note` to every other connection. A rejected put is acked
with `accepted:false` and the stored note is sent back to the sender as `note`
so it can adopt it. `created_at` is kept from the first version.

## Client behaviour (reference: Notes module)

- Keep notes in a local SQLite DB; the app works fully offline.
- Track `last_seq` (highest applied server seq) and a per-note `dirty` flag.
- Debounce local edits (~400 ms) then send `put`; clear `dirty` on `ack accepted` for
  that id if the note was not edited again meanwhile.
- On (re)connect: `hello{since:last_seq}`, apply snapshot, then re-send all dirty notes.
- Applying a remote note: if the local copy is not dirty → overwrite. If dirty and
  remote `updated_at` is newer → adopt remote (LWW), keeping the cursor position if the
  note is open. Otherwise keep local and (re)send it.
- Reconnect with exponential backoff (1 s … 60 s). If WebSocket upgrade keeps failing
  (e.g. a corporate proxy), fall back to REST polling `GET /v1/notes?since=` every 10 s
  and `PUT` for writes.

## Config (client)

Config section `notes.sync` in `~/.config/bento/config.json`:

```json
"sync": { "enabled": true, "server": "https://bento.radian.dk", "tokenFile": "~/.config/bento/sync-token" }
```

The token file contains only the token (mode 600) and is never written into config.json.
